name: mp3check
desc: Tool to check mp3 files for consistency
why: Inspects MP3 frame structure for consistency, a small window into how the file format is actually laid out.

brief.what_it_is: mp3check is a command-line tool, installed as the executable mp3check, that checks MP3 files for consistency. The scout notes describe it as inspecting MP3 frame structure. The homepage and the wiki page I tried both returned only a Google Code Archive shell that requires JavaScript, so I could not read the README or any documentation. The description in the Homebrew formula is 'Tool to check mp3 files for consistency.'
brief.why_it_exists: Not confirmed. The Homebrew description says only that it checks MP3 files for consistency; the author's own framing was not reachable.
brief.how_it_works: Not confirmed from the source. The scout notes say it inspects MP3 frame structure for consistency, which suggests it walks the file's frames and checks that their headers agree with each other, but I could not verify that against any documentation.
brief.install_notes: Installed via Homebrew under the formula name mp3check, which provides the mp3check executable. The formula has no caveats. I did not find any notes on runtimes, configuration, or first-run steps because the documentation pages did not load.
brief.standout: Per the scout notes, it is a small window into how the MP3 file format is laid out at the frame level, which makes it useful for seeing the format rather than only playing audio. I could not confirm this from the project's own pages.
brief.status: unknown. The Google Code project is hosted in the Google Code Archive, which is the read-only long-term storage for the former Google Code Project Hosting service, so active development there has stopped. I found no release date or commit information because the archive page did not render.
brief.caveats: The homepage and the wiki page I tried were both unreadable without JavaScript, so this brief rests only on the Homebrew description and scout notes. Google Code shut down in 2016, so the project is archived and the source may not be easy to find elsewhere. Platform support, licensing, and the exact checks performed are unknown.
